record.paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
record.original_question: Let D be a finite digraph with minimum out-degree k. Must D contain k directed cycles C1, C2, ..., Ck that can be ordered so that, for every j at most k, the union of the earlier cycles C1, ..., Cj-1 and the cycle Cj have at most one vertex in common?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.2 Every digraph D of minimum out-degree k contains a sequence C1, C2, . . . , Ck of cycles such that Sj−1 i=1 Ci and Cj have at most one vertex in common for all j ≤ k.
Conjecture 3.2 was proved for tournaments by Havet, Thomass´e and Yeo [48]. However, there is much less progress in our understanding of Conjecture 3.2 than of Conjecture 3.1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D=(V,E)$ be a finite directed graph (loops and multiple arcs disallowed) such that every vertex has out-degree at least $k$, where $k\ge 1$ is an integer. A directed cycle in $D$ is a sequence $v_0\to v_1\to\cdots\to v_{\ell-1}\to v_0$ of distinct vertices with each consecutive arc in $E$.

Prove or disprove: there exist $k$ directed cycles $C_1,C_2,\ldots,C_k$ in $D$ (not necessarily distinct as cycles, but ordered) such that for every $j$ with $2\le j\le k$,
$$\Bigl|V(C_j)\cap\bigcup_{i=1}^{j-1}V(C_i)\Bigr|\le 1,$$
i.e., the cycle $C_j$ shares at most one vertex with the union of the vertex sets of the previously chosen cycles.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (Hoàng–Reed) is known to hold for tournaments (Havet–Thomassé–Yeo) and for digraphs with minimum out-degree at most 3 (the δ+=2 case follows from Thomassen, and the δ+=3 case was established by Bang-Jensen, Bessy and Thomassé). The general case for arbitrary k remains open.
